Subject: Post-demo: ClearHealth security follow-ups & retention clarifications

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the security/compliance items you raised (SOC 2 / data lifecycle / vendor questionnaire):

1) SOC 2 status
- Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report for our hosted platform (most recent period ended 2026-06). We can share the report under an NDA.

2) Data retention & deletion SLAs
- Default log retention: 90 days (configurable).
- Backups: rolling snapshots retained for 30 days by default. For regulated workloads we offer extended retention options under Dedicated/Private (examples: 1 year, 7 years).
- Delete/erase requests: application-level deletion is executed within 48 hours; snapshots and backups are removed according to the retention window and are eligible for expedited deletion requests (see note below).

3) Backup/restore & evidence
- Backups are encrypted at rest with customer-facing KMS options for Private deployments. We can provide an evidence bundle (audit timestamp + snapshot IDs + deletion ops log) for completed erasure requests.

4) Vendor security questionnaire
- Attaching a short VSQ template we typically ask customers to complete. If you prefer, we can intake via secure portal or schedule a short call to go line-by-line.

Proposed next steps:
- Samantha: confirm whether you want the SOC 2 report (we will send NDA link) and who should complete the VSQ on your side.
- Redwood (Monica + Ben): prepare a short write-up of the retention deletion flow and sample evidence package we can provide for an erase request.

Attaching: Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_Template.docx; SOC2_Overview.pdf (summary).

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min follow-up tomorrow if that helps.

—Rachel

Rachel —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our security team: 

- ClearHealth needs to understand the maximum retention for user-identifiable logs (we're governed by HIPAA for a subset of records). Is there an upper limit restriction for hosted customers?
- When you say "expedited deletion requests" for backups, can you confirm an SLA for full removal of all copies (including off-host snapshots / provider-managed replication)? Our security policy needs a worst-case timeline.
- We will complete the VSQ but we'd like to record any exceptions as "operational constraints" up front — can you confirm if Redwood uses customer-managed KMS for hosted plans or only for Private deployments?

Victor (cc) is our security lead — he'll handle the VSQ. Please send the NDA link for SOC2. Also, what evidence looks like for a deletion event? Timestamp + snapshot IDs is a good start but do you provide hashes or hash manifests to show a file was deleted?

Thanks,
Samantha

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: ClearHealth security follow-ups & retention clarifications

Hi Samantha / Victor —

Thanks for the follow-ups. Short answers and operational detail below (I tried to keep this tight; happy to expand on any bullet):

- Retention limits (hosted): there is no hard technical "cap" preventing longer retention, but hosted customers are on a shared platform and longer retention increases cost. Typical hosted default is 90-day logs / 30-day backups. We can offer contractually committed retention windows (1 year / 7 years) via a Dedicated or Private plan or as an add-on to an enterprise hosted agreement.

- Expedited deletion SLA (backups / provider replication):
  * Application-layer records: removed within 48 hours of request (we log the operation).
  * Snapshots/backups: standard propagation means some snapshots may persist up to the configured backup TTL; for expedited deletion we initiate a prioritized workflow — target full removal within 7 calendar days for hosted customers, and 48–72 hours for Dedicated/Private where we control the storage lifecycle. We will document snapshot IDs and deletion operation IDs in the evidence package.

- Evidence artifacts we can provide:
  * Deletion confirmation email with timestamp and operator id.
  * Snapshot IDs and storage object keys removed.
  * Audit log entries referencing the erase operation (w/ redaction where required).
  * For Private deployments with customer-managed KMS: we can provide KMS rotation and key-destruction timelines as additional proof.
  * We do not release raw storage hashes externally for security reasons, but we can provide signed manifests (hashes over a signed manifest) under a mutual NDA if required for your audit.

- KMS options:
  * Hosted: encryption at rest with provider-managed keys by default. Customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) is available for Dedicated and Private.

Next steps I suggest:
- Rachel: I can prepare a 1-page "Retention & Deletion: ClearHealth evidence template" that maps the artifacts we can provide to typical audit questions.
- Samantha / Victor: if you send the completed VSQ we can mark any true exceptions and propose compensating controls.

If useful, we can schedule a 30-minute technical dive with our infra engineer to walk through retention lifecycle and show an example evidence bundle (redacted).

—Ben
